scope: Phase 2 first eight Hays candidate diagnostic source verification cohort
primary_regional_flora: Flora of North Central Texas (user Library file; actual Flora pages read this pass)
complementary_regional_flora: Hagenbuch & Lemke (2015) Vegetative Key to Grasses of Texas Hill Country
historical_nomenclature_rule: If regional Flora uses historical Coelorachis/Tridens names preserve original treatment, but stage Kew accepted name; not evidence that broad old taxon is identical to modern split.
difference_between_states: source_supported_morphology describes expected characters in species, whereas actually_visible_in_hays_photo_review records observation-level evidence. If not directly visible and authenticated, the Lab key state remains unapproved.
photo_license_rule: Potential eligible licenses need current exact-photo reconfirmation and intended website-rights assessment; no source images were downloaded in this pass.

source_key.reference: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon 1999. Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas, Poaceae

source_supported_morphology.description: Rhizomatous perennial, typically 50–120 cm tall
Branched flowering panicle with elongated spikelets; published length '10–26 mm' appears inconsistent with habit and is not used as a field threshold
Spikelets about 8–15 mm with usually 2–3 fertile florets
Terminal sterile florets/rudiments are narrow and not divergent from the rachilla; contrast M. mutica spreading, broadly obovate rudiments
Membranous ligule 3–6 mm, sheath nearly closed to throat (regional 2015 vegetative key)

taxa.actually_visible_in_hays_photo_review: Loose panicle branches with pendulous pale spikelets, leaf blades and tussock context; some hand-scaled flowering heads.
taxa.not_demonstrated_in_hays_photo_review: Fertile-floret count and sterile-rudiment shape not resolved; glume inequality and inner ligule dimensions not measurable.
taxa.prioritized_next_evidence: Show one complete spikelet with fertile floret count and terminal rudiments, and a separate 1-mm-scaled ligule photo.
taxa.caveat: Possible typo in 1999 Flora panicle length; do not encode the reported 'mm' panicle value without independent confirmation.

source_key.reference: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon 1999. Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas, Poaceae

source_supported_morphology.description: Perennial with hard base, short knotty rhizomes, erect or arching culms 25–100 cm
Short membranous ligule about 0.5–1 mm
Very slender cylindrical spike-like raceme about 3 mm in diameter; axis breaks apart at joints
Rachis joints have niches in which spikelets fit tightly
Pairs include sessile fertile spikelet with pitted glume and pedicelled sterile spikelet

taxa.actually_visible_in_hays_photo_review: Very narrow pencil-like cylindrical inflorescence with obvious successive nodes/segment pattern and hand scale; erect to arching culms and natural grassy habitat in several independent observations.
taxa.not_demonstrated_in_hays_photo_review: Sessile spikelet rachis-niche architecture, pitted glume and exact membrane ligule cannot be resolved in photographs; confirm with dissection before final species-ID signoff.
taxa.prioritized_next_evidence: Isolate one rachis segment showing its niche and sessile/pedicelled spikelet pair with a scale.
taxa.caveat: Current Kew accepted genus differs from 1999 Flora; preserve Coelorachis/Mnesithea historical names.

source_key.reference: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon 1999. Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas, Poaceae

source_supported_morphology.description: Tufted perennial approximately 30–100 cm tall; leaf blades about 7–18 mm broad
Usually 2–5 spike-like branches 4–8 cm long
Paired/closely arranged spikelets 2.2–2.6 mm in regional Flora (FNA reports broader variation)
First/lower glume present on some or all spikelets
Second/upper glume and sterile lemma pubescent, including papillose-based hairs in FNA account

taxa.actually_visible_in_hays_photo_review: Several slender racemes on branched flowering stalks, paired rows of spikelets in macro view, strap-like basal leaves, wooded/rocky ground context in some observations.
taxa.not_demonstrated_in_hays_photo_review: First-glume presence and dark brown glandular blotches on second glume/sterile lemma cannot be verified at this review scale; species identification unproven.
taxa.prioritized_next_evidence: Examine original TEX00568501 spikelets at 10×–20× for the lower glume and pubescence, comparing co-collected P. pubiflorum.
taxa.lookalikes: Paspalum pubiflorum (lower glume absent), P. distichum

taxa.caveat: Three original TEX Hays sheets inspected but minute hairs and lower glume not independently resolved; 2019 yard specimen has cultivation uncertainty.

source_key.reference: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon 1999. Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas, Poaceae

source_supported_morphology.description: Annual up to about 100 cm, leaf blades generally 3–10 mm wide
Leaf sheaths somewhat compressed
Soft, flexible flowering head with usually green bristles
Spikelets about 1.8–2.6 mm
Fertile lemma very finely wrinkled/rugose

taxa.actually_visible_in_hays_photo_review: Bottlebrush-like narrow fuzzy panicles, often green but some tan, and visible radiating bristles, clumped annual-looking plants.
taxa.not_demonstrated_in_hays_photo_review: Short-burst bristle arrangement and finely rugose fertile lemma are not resolved against Setaria pumila, S. parviflora and other foxtails; many closeup images of head but no spikelet dissections.
taxa.prioritized_next_evidence: Verify mature fertile lemma surface, 1–2 mm hair-fringe ligule, and an annual fibrous root system on same plant.
taxa.lookalikes: Setaria leucopila (perennial), S. pumila, S. parviflora
taxa.caveat: Introduced Eurasian grass in Flora, appropriate to identify but not a native restoration planting recommendation.

source_key.reference: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon 1999. Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas, Poaceae

source_supported_morphology.description: Tufted perennial, about 20–100 cm tall
Bristles typically about 4–15 mm long
Fertile lemma finely rugose with transverse wrinkles
Vegetative key notes hairiness around sheath throat and hair-fringe ligule

taxa.actually_visible_in_hays_photo_review: Very narrow cylindrical green flowering heads with short bristles, basal leafy tussocks and flowering culms with hand scale.
taxa.not_demonstrated_in_hays_photo_review: Bristle length only approximate, maturity and perennial rhizomatous/tufted base uncertain; fertile lemma fine rugosity/wrinkles unresolvable.
taxa.prioritized_next_evidence: Document perennial crown, short sheaths/ligule hairs, actual bristle lengths, and fertile lemma wrinkles.
taxa.caveat: Setaria vegetative differences can be subtle; measure same-specimen morphology rather than inferring species solely from head.

source_key.reference: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon 1999. Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas, Poaceae

source_supported_morphology.description: Coarse grass typically 1–2 m tall, often in low moist habitat
Sheaths typically with rough/hispid papilla-based hairs, especially toward summit
Spikelets about 3–5 mm excluding awn, with or without papilla-based hairs
Lower floret lemma awn often 1.5–6 cm long; occasionally shortened or absent

taxa.actually_visible_in_hays_photo_review: Well-displayed branched awned inflorescences, broad leaf blades, markedly hairy/papillose sheaths in closeups, and wetland edge habitat; multiple independent observations.
taxa.not_demonstrated_in_hays_photo_review: Awn and papilla-based sheath hairs strongly favor Walter's barnyardgrass, but the critical lower floret lemma/awn origin, glume size and comparison with E. crus-galli are not fully measured.
taxa.prioritized_next_evidence: Photograph mature spikelet with awn origin and adjacent sheath hairs showing papilla-like raised hair bases.
taxa.lookalikes: Echinochloa crus-galli, E. muricata, other barnyardgrasses
taxa.caveat: Not every E. walteri has long awns; absence of long awn cannot automatically exclude.

source_key.reference: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon 1999. Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas, Poaceae

source_supported_morphology.description: Annual with single or tufted culms about 15–100(120) cm
Membranous ligule around 1.5–3 mm long
Narrow dense spike-like flowering panicle
Shiny, usually 2–3-flowered spikelets about 1.5–5 mm long
Second/upper glume broadly obovate, blunt at apex (unlike Koeleria)

taxa.actually_visible_in_hays_photo_review: Narrow erect densely flowered spikes/panicles, tan maturing flowers, green panicle heads, a close sheath/leaf junction and multiple independent field scenes.
taxa.not_demonstrated_in_hays_photo_review: Second glume wide obovate blunt apex, floret arrangement and distinction from Koeleria or other wedgescales cannot be proven from contact-size images.
taxa.prioritized_next_evidence: Isolate and photograph second glume broad blunt face, plus floret count and measured true inner ligule.
taxa.caveat: Gross dense panicle does not establish correct Sphenopholis species.

source_key.reference: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon 1999. Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas, Poaceae

source_supported_morphology.description: Roughly 20–80 cm in the broad Tridens muticus account, narrow elongated 7–20(25) cm panicle
Var. elongatus: second glume usually 3–7 nerved and about 6–8 mm long
Leaves usually 3–4 mm wide in elongatus concept
Var. muticus: usually single-veined second glume around 5 mm or shorter, blades typically 1–2 mm wide

taxa.actually_visible_in_hays_photo_review: Exceptionally useful Hays photos: small tuft, long narrow panicles, scaly overlapping spikelets, partial collar/ligule, mature branches in hand.
taxa.not_demonstrated_in_hays_photo_review: Species boundary versus Tridentopsis mutica and T. buckleyana depends on lemma/callus, florets, ligule and anther dimensions not all reliably measured.
taxa.prioritized_next_evidence: Backlight one isolated upper glume, count all nerves and measure length, then compare against verified T. mutica.
